meta.title: Do Plants Like Music?
meta.textType: a school science text with an experiment

paragraphs: Do Plants Like Music, posted by Leo. Our class studies plants this term. The classroom has a big window, and the sun comes in all morning. Teacher Kim asked a strange question, "Do plants like music?" I laughed first, but then I wanted to know too. The whole class wanted to find out. So we made an experiment. Every group made a plan, and we wrote it in our notebooks.

We put two beans in two cups of earth. We chose a bean, because a bean grows fast. We wrote a number on each cup, one and two. We gave both cups the same water and the same sun. We put the cups on the same window. Next to cup two, we put a pair of headphones. The headphones played soft music for one hour every day. The music was soft, because loud music can be bad for ears. Cup one had no headphones, so it stayed quiet. Mia watered both plants at the same time. She used a small bottle, and she poured the same amount.

Every Monday, we measured both plants with a ruler in centimeters. We wrote the numbers in order, from week one to week four. The plants grew a little every day, but we could not see it. In week one, both plants were three centimeters tall. In week two, plant one was five centimeters, and plant two was six. In week three, plant one was seven centimeters, and plant two was nine. In week four, plant one was nine centimeters, and plant two was twelve. Mia wrote all the numbers in the record of the class. On the last Monday, the whole class stood around the window.

We discovered that the plant with music was taller. Mia asked, "Does the music really help?" Teacher Kim smiled and said, "We do not know yet." But Teacher Kim said, "One experiment is not enough." The music may help the plant to grow. It might also be that bean two was a stronger bean. A good scientist does the test again and again. "Then you can believe the numbers," she said.
Next month, we will do the experiment again with six cups. Mia will record the numbers, and I will draw the plants. Maybe plants like music, or maybe they like my drawings. What do you think?
text.summary: Leo writes about a class experiment with two bean plants. One plant has music from headphones, and the whole class measures both plants in centimeters for four weeks and records the numbers in order.
